primary_topics: Keynote address at the launch of Senator Jovito R. Salonga's book 'Not By Power or Wealth Alone,' August 14, 2007 -- CJP wrote the Foreword and was asked to deliver the launch address; 'his invitation is really a command, a direct order from a superior'

The book's governing thesis: Salonga has had power, wealth, fame and fortune, but declares them 'thoroughly inadequate to satisfy life and to reform society' -- the overriding constancy was God's all-abiding presence

The 1986 dissolution of Salonga's law firm: when recruited by Cory Aquino, he didn't merely take a leave of absence as law and ethics demanded -- he 'dissolved permanently the Salonga Ordonez Yap and Associates Law Office'; chose to 'live simply so that others may simply live'

The 2007 Ramon Magsaysay Award: 'considered by many as the Asian Nobel Prize'; awarded for 'exemplary integrity and substance of his long public career in service to democracy and good government in the Philippines'
sub_topics: CJP's dual role: wrote the Foreword to the book AND delivers the launch address; 'his invitation is really a command, a direct order from a superior'
Book title as summation: 'Not by Power or Wealth Alone is its best summation'
God's constancy: 'in all these, the overriding constancy was the all-abiding presence of God in everything he did, said or wrote'

The 1986 law firm dissolution: 'when he and his law partners were recruited to public office by President Corazon C. Aquino in 1986, Dr. Salonga was not satisfied with taking a leave from his prestigious law firm as demanded by law and ethics; he went all the way and dissolved permanently the Salonga Ordonez Yap and Associates Law Office. He chose to forego the luxuries that wealth could buy to be able to demonstrate the virtues that power and wealth alone could not bring, like integrity, honor and dignity. He chose to live simply so that others may simply live.'

Teaching by example: 'a dedicated husband, a caring father, a faithful friend and a devoted man of God. Never compromising his values and principles in exchange for friendship, kinship, relationship, power or wealth, he lives an almost ascetic life. He does not smoke, does not drink, and does not gamble.'

Two laws: 'his love for and dedication to the rule of law is exemplified by two laws he sponsored: the Anti-Plunder Law and the Anti-Coup D'Etat Law. While he is passionate about reforms, he is equally determined to pursue them only through legal methods.'

Ramon Magsaysay Award 2007: 'for the exemplary integrity and substance of his long public career in service to democracy and good government in the Philippines. This grand award, considered by many as the Asian Nobel Prize, is the latest in a long list of honors'
Different faiths, same values: 'though we are of different faiths, he a staunch Protestant and me a fledgling Catholic, we never talked of what divided us but only of what brought us together'

Salonga's theology: 'worship and life could not be separated. The man who seeks to be a Christian when he is at prayer or attending worship must be equally Christian when he is out in the world, in the field of relations between individuals, groups or nations.'

At 87, still carrying shrapnel: 'despite his advanced age and despite the many tiny pieces of shrapnel still imbedded in his frail body as a result of that grenade blast in Plaza Miranda, he is still sprightly. More important, his intellect and his interest in public welfare are still as sharp as when he was 40.'

Closing tribute: 'our Good Lord had granted him a long and purposeful life, because He wanted him to be the conscience of the nation; to be its fearless anchor during stormy seas of political upheavals; and to be the indefatigable teacher and model of the young and not-so-young who aspire to lead this country.'

stances.claim: Salonga's 1986 decision to dissolve permanently his law firm -- rather than merely taking a leave of absence as legally required -- is the governing proof of the book's thesis: power and wealth alone are insufficient; integrity, honor and dignity (things money cannot buy) are what endure. The dissolution was not required; it was chosen, making it the most consequential voluntary sacrifice of personal advantage in CJP's social circle.
stances.rhetorical_move: dissolution-as-thesis-proof: the beyond-minimum-requirement law firm dissolution as the definitive behavioral evidence of the book's governing principle

stances.claim: Salonga at 87 -- carrying Plaza Miranda shrapnel, still sprightly, 'his intellect and interest in public welfare still as sharp as when he was 40' -- is God's most tangible gift to the nation: 'our Good Lord had granted him a long and purposeful life, because He wanted him to be the conscience of the nation.' Longevity as divine commission.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered August 14, 2007 at the launch of Senator Jovito R. Salonga's 'Not By Power or Wealth Alone' -- CJP wrote the Foreword and was asked to deliver the launch address: 'his invitation is really a command, a direct order from a superior' -- this address distills the book's governing thesis: Salonga has had power, wealth, fame and fortune in his long career, but declares them 'thoroughly inadequate to satisfy life and to reform society'; 'the overriding constancy was the all-abiding presence of God in everything he did, said or wrote.' The defining proof of the thesis: when Cory Aquino recruited Salonga in 1986, he didn't merely take a leave of absence as law and ethics demanded -- 'he went all the way and dissolved permanently the Salonga Ordonez Yap and Associates Law Office. He chose to live simply so that others may simply live.' He teaches by example: dedicated husband, caring father, faithful friend, devoted man of God; 'never compromising his values and principles in exchange for friendship, kinship, relationship, power or wealth, he lives an almost ascetic life.' Two laws he sponsored: the Anti-Plunder Law and the Anti-Coup D'Etat Law; 'while he is passionate about reforms, he is equally determined to pursue them only through legal methods.' The 2007 Ramon Magsaysay Award -- 'considered by many as the Asian Nobel Prize' -- was awarded 'for the exemplary integrity and substance of his long public career in service to democracy and good government.' Interfaith note: 'though we are of different faiths, he a staunch Protestant and me a fledgling Catholic, we never talked of what divided us but only of what brought us together.' At 87, 'despite the many tiny pieces of shrapnel still imbedded in his frail body as a result of that grenade blast in Plaza Miranda, he is still sprightly... his intellect and interest in public welfare are still as sharp as when he was 40.' Closing: God granted him a long life 'because He wanted him to be the conscience of the nation; to be its fearless anchor during stormy seas; and to be the indefatigable teacher and model of the young and not-so-young who aspire to lead this country.'
